command: SSH inventory; remove the user-owned uv-tool installation; verify exact private-draft checksums; fresh binary install through a loopback-only release fixture; verify receipt, shell resolution, doctor manager probes, and preserved config
decisions: The user-owned prior uv-tool installation was removed before the fresh installation; configuration and sessions were preserved.
A root-owned global npm 0.11.0 command was discovered and retained because non-interactive sudo correctly refused removal without a password.
The exact draft Linux x86_64 binary was verified on both machines with SHA-256 6a6dc0e5a209629a1e53dfc23612c4b1912b9b6335fe80d17cc073d5d67ea46a before activation.
The installer returned documented status 10 because the invoking SSH parent still resolved the root npm command, while fresh login and interactive shells resolved the verified user binary.
The installed canonical receipt recorded binary method, v1.0.5, Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35, active-path match, skipped setup, and the exact activation state.

Offline doctor completed without the prior frozen-runtime GLIBCXX failure; npm-prefix and npm-root external manager probes returned ok, the new command was active, and the root npm path was reported as shadowed.

The existing configuration SHA-256 remained byte-identical before and after installation. Doctor exit 1 was an honest readiness result because Codex CLI/auth and the selected model route were not configured, not an installation failure.
errors: The root-owned global npm installation could not be removed with sudo -n because the host requires an interactive administrator password; it was left unchanged and reported as a collision.
result: The exact v1.0.5 draft binary fresh-installed transactionally on Ubuntu 22.04/glibc 2.35 after removing the user-owned prior version, preserved user data, resolved first in fresh shells, and safely diagnosed the remaining root npm collision plus incomplete auth/model readiness.
limitations: The authenticated private-draft files were served from a loopback-only fixture because draft release URLs are not anonymously accessible before promotion.
The root-owned npm 0.11.0 command remains until the operator runs sudo npm uninstall -g jarn-cli interactively.
First-time ChatGPT authentication and live model selection were not run, so this record does not claim UAT-001 or auth/model readiness.
